newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end down, US rate fears stoked by Fed.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end down, US rate fears stoked by Fed.

text.p: Dutch shares slipped in afternoon trade on Tuesday as Wall Street sold off on renewed interest rate concerns in the U.S.

A senior Fed source said eight of 12 regional Fed banks had requested a hike in the 5.0 percent discount rate amid mounting evidence the pace of U.S. expansion is likely to remain brisk in the second half of 1996.
The AEX index closed down 3.90 points at 564.27.
U.S. August industrial production and capacity utilization data was seen not swaying the Fed in its interest rate deliberations.
Industrial production rose 0.5 percent versus an expected 0.4 percent rise, and capacity utilization was 83.5 percent versus an expected 83.3 percent.
Dealers said there was very little reaction to the 1997 Dutch budget as most of the news had already been leaked.
"There might be some impact tomorrow after investors digest what's in the papers, but it will be limited," one dealer said.
Unilever shares shed 4.70 guilders to 265.10 on profit taking and concern over ice-cream sales.
Broker Kleinwort Benson said it had reiterated its "sell" on the stock after limp results from fellow ice-cream maker Treats.
Heineken managed to rack up its first gain since Friday's shock profit warning sent shares plummeting over 16 percent. "There was some short covering today," one dealer said.
The stock closed up 2.00 guilders at 305.00 after touching 315.00 guilders earlier in the session.
Some dealers said the stock could go as low as 280 to 290 guilders, with others looking for it to stay around the 300 guilder mark.
Philips got a boost after positive comments from Intel late yesterday were seen helping the entire semiconductor sector. The firm said Q3 revenues were running better than expected.
Investors also welcomed yesterday's comments from Philips that problems in introducing new DVD technology were close to being resolved. The stock closed up 1.80 guilders at 57.50.
